name: LingBot-VLA 2.0
summary: LingBot-VLA 2.0 is Ant Group's open cross-embodiment policy, a 6B checkpoint on a Qwen3-VL-4B backbone with a Mixture-of-Experts action expert. Its organising idea is a unified 55-dimensional canonical action space into which arms, grippers, dexterous hands and mobile bases are all projected, so one model controls all of them without per-embodiment heads. MoE routing uses the auxiliary-loss-free strategy from DeepSeek-V3, and training adds dual-query distillation supervised by two teachers, LingBot-Depth and DINO-Video, to make the policy future-aware. It was trained on roughly 60,000 hours spanning 20 robot configurations, reports 66.2/34.4 progress/success on the GM-100 generalist benchmark on AgileX Cobot Magic, and is released under Apache-2.0 with weights, code and a technical report.
innovation: A single canonical action space wide enough to absorb grippers, dexterous hands and mobile bases, replacing per-embodiment action heads.
MoE action expert with auxiliary-loss-free routing imported from language-model practice.
Dual-query distillation from depth and video teachers to inject future-awareness without a separate world model.
matters: The most permissively licensed cross-embodiment VLA at this scale; LeRobot 0.6 carries it as a stock policy, which is how open models become defaults.
limits: GM-100 success rate of 34.4 shows how far generalist policies still are from reliability, whatever the progress score says.
60,000 hours across 20 configurations is heavily weighted toward the platforms Ant has access to.
lineage: Cross-embodiment training in the RT-X tradition, rebuilt on an open VLM backbone with a canonical action space.
